She stressed the need for initiatives such as cyclone shelters with separate facilities for women and improved access to reproductive and mental healthcare.
Shama also underscored that gender-responsive climate action should not be limited to one-off projects but must be embedded in the way resilience initiatives are planned, financed, implemented, and monitored.
"When women lead and participate fully, our communities become more resilient, and our future becomes more secure," she said.

item.title: UDJFB condemns torture of three DT journalists in Tongi
item.description:
The Urban Development Journalists Forum Bangladesh (UDJFB) has strongly condemned the hostage-taking, torture and death threats against three journalists, including Dhaka Tribune reporter Rabiul Hasan, who were attacked while investigating drug trafficking in Tongi, Gazipur.
Rabiul Hasan is a member of the UDJFB. The other two journalists targeted in the attack were reporter Asiful Islam Rifat and photojournalist Abir Ahmed Shupto.
In a joint statement issued on Thursday, UDJFB President Matin Abdullah and General Secretary Hasan Emon condemned the incident and demanded the immediate arrest and exemplary punishment of those responsible.
According to the statement, the three journalists went to Haji Mazar slum, under Tongi West police station, on November 6 to investigate drug trafficking as part of their professional duties. They spent around one and a half hours at the location, gathering evidence and recording video footage of alleged drug transactions.
At one stage, a group of 20 to 25 armed alleged drug traders, who had been monitoring their movements through CCTV cameras, attacked the journalists.
The attackers allegedly pointed pistols at their heads, threatened to mutilate them with sharp weapons and snatched Rabiul Hasan's mobile phone before deleting all the evidence and information they had collected.
The journalists were then taken to a nearby location and held captive for around three hours. During this time, they were brutally beaten and allegedly subjected to an attempt on their lives through gunfire.
The attackers also allegedly forced the journalists to consume a sedative and recorded videos with money and drugs placed in front of them, apparently to use the footage for blackmail.
They were eventually released after being threatened with death and warned against publishing reports on the group's drug trade and other criminal activities, the statement said.
The injured journalists subsequently received medical treatment at Shaheed Ahsan Ullah Master General Hospital in Tongi.
Expressing grave concern over repeated attacks on journalists at a location it described as a haven for criminals, the forum said such acts of violence and intimidation were aimed at silencing independent and investigative journalism.
The UDJFB said attempts by organised criminal groups to suppress factual reporting and intimidate journalists through violence threatened not only press freedom but also democratic values and freedom of expression.
The forum said the local administration and law enforcement agencies could not evade responsibility for the attack on the three journalists.
It called for an immediate crackdown in Haji Mazar slum and surrounding areas to arrest the alleged masterminds and armed attackers and bring them to justice.
The forum also urged the relevant authorities to ensure adequate security for the three journalists.
The statement was signed by Latiful Islam, office secretary of the Urban Development Journalists Forum Bangladesh (UDJFB).

item.title: Rizvi: Hasina must be extradited, not welcomed with flowers
item.description:
BNP acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Friday said ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina will have to be brought back to Bangladesh through the existing extradition treaty with India, stressing that she must not be welcomed as if she were returning from a visit to her parents' or in-laws' home.
“Many people have been killed, and numerous cases have been filed against Sheikh Hasina. She has also been convicted and sentenced to death for crimes against humanity. Yet, discussions about bringing her back make it sound as if she had gone to her parents’ or in-laws’ home and should be welcomed with flowers,” he said.
Rizvi said Hasina would have to be brought back in accordance with the provisions of the extradition treaty between Bangladesh and India and through the ongoing judicial and legal processes.
He made the remarks while addressing a discussion organised by the Jatiyatabadi Mohila Dal at the Jatiya Press Club, marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day.
Referring to Hasina’s intention to return to Bangladesh and her reportedly application for a passport, visa and national identity card, the BNP leader said there is no scope for her to be repatriated. “Only extradition is an option for her,” he said.
Explaining the difference, he said extradition is a legal matter between two countries, while repatriation applies to someone who has left their country without facing any allegations and later wishes to return.
“If I leave my country without any allegations against me and later want to return, I can apply to my own country for a passport if I do not have one. But can the same process can apply to someone facing criminal cases, state prosecution and sentences in their own country? Such a person is subject to extradition,” Rizvi said.
Bangladesh has an extradition treaty with India, making Hasina’s return a legal matter between the two countries, he said.
The BNP leader said Hasina killed around 1,400 people, including students and rickshaw-pullers, during the July 2024 mass uprising. “Several cases are pending against her, and she has already been sentenced in some cases, including a death sentence.”
“Why is all this fanfare over her return? She must face the ongoing trials in Bangladesh and serve the sentences handed down to her,” he said.
Turning to the role of women in politics, Rizvi said women leaders and activists of the BNP had played a significant role in the struggle for democracy during the past 17 years.
He recalled how police repeatedly erected barricades to prevent their programmes and how women activists tried to break through them despite fear of arrest, enforced disappearance and harassment.
Bangladesh wants Hasina, who faces the death penalty, to be extradited from India under the existing extradition treaty, while India has said travel documents are required for people to travel.
Hasina fled to India after student-led protests had forced her from power on August 5, 2024 and had since then remained there.
In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity committed during the mass uprising.

item.title: Dengue claims 2 more lives, 1,255 hospitalised in 24hrs
item.description:
Two more people died of dengue and 1,255 were hospitalised across the country in the 24 hours until 8am on Friday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The latest fatalities have raised the death toll from the mosquito-borne disease to 483 this year.
Of the newly hospitalised patients, 434 were in Dhaka Division, 267 in Chittagong, 160 in Khulna, 147 in Barisal, 89 in Rajshahi, 76 each in Mymensingh and Rangpur, and six in Sylhet.
A total of 158,883 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals nationwide so far this year. Of them, 152,485 have recovered and returned home.
Last year, 102,861 people were infected with dengue and 413 died from the disease.

item.title: Klopp asks for time in Germany rebuild
item.description:
Germany coach Jurgen Klopp on Thursday dismissed talk his squad lacked talent but asked for more time to improve the four-time world champions after poor results at major tournaments over the past decade.
Klopp took over from Julian Nagelsmann in the summer after Germany were knocked out by Paraguay at the last-32 stage of the World Cup.
It was Germany's third straight early exit from the tournament, after group stage eliminations in 2018 and 2022.
Speaking in Belgrade ahead of Friday's Nations League clash with Serbia, Klopp said he was confident in the talent at his disposal and said the players needed time together.
"It is very often said that German football is lacking in many areas -- including the number of good players, great talents, world-class players, and so on," said Klopp.
"But I have a super positive outlook on this team. To be honest, we have a very good mix."
Klopp, 59, said he was not "naive or wide-eyed -- we're genuinely very good... we just need to make that visible, to translate it onto the pitch."
The former Liverpool manager also asked for time when taking over at Anfield, saying he needed to turn everyone at the fallen English giants from "doubter to believer" to restore the club to their former glory.
"I have to allow myself the time," Klopp said Thursday, but added: "if this suits the public, that's not something I can control.
"We are on the right path -- though we are, of course, still a long way from the end. The foundation, however, is genuinely good."
Klopp praised Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz, who has been in better form in recent weeks.
"Flo (Wirtz) is in top condition. He can be an immense help to us," Klopp said.
Wirtz has come under fire since his big-money move to Liverpool in 2025, but he has improved under new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola.
He has three assists in his past four Premier League games and scored his first league goal of the season in Sunday's 3-1 win at Crystal Palace.
The former Bayer Leverkusen player is still just 23 but could play his 50th match for Germany on Monday in Berlin.
Wirtz felt the team was improving under Klopp and said he wanted to take on a greater leadership role in the young squad.
"I feel like we've gelled even better and solidified the things we've been working on in training. It comes down to bringing will, conviction, and passion onto the pitch," Wirtz said Thursday.

item.title: Messi finalist for third straight MLS MVP award
item.description:
Lionel Messi is among the finalists for the 2026 Major League Soccer Most Valuable Player award, putting the Argentine superstar in line for an unprecedented third straight MVP honor.
The Inter Miami captain was named MVP in 2024 and 2025, becoming the second player to win the trophy twice after Preki, who won it in 1997 and 2003.
Messi, 39, was the top scorer in the regular season with 26 goals in 31 matches for Miami, who will be chasing a second straight title when the playoffs begin next week.
The other MVP finalists are German playmaker Hany Mukhtar of Nashville SC, Brazilians Evander of FC Cincinnati and Guilherme of Houston Dynamo, and American Cavan Sullivan of Philadelphia Union, this season's revelation at just 17 years old.
Sullivan, who scored nine goals in 29 matches, is also a finalist for Young Player of the Year alongside New York Red Bull's Julian Hall and Adri Mehmeti.

item.title: Pegula beats Noskova to advance at WTA Finals, knock out Gauff
item.description:
Jessica Pegula saved a match point on the way to a three-set victory over Linda Noskova on Thursday to book her WTA Finals last-four berth as Coco Gauff was eliminated.
Fifth-ranked American Pegula fired a career-high 16 aces to come up with a 7-6 (7/2), 4-6, 7-5 victory in the must-win match against Wimbledon champion Noskova.
Her triumph, in the final group one round-robin match, meant world number four Gauff was eliminated from the elite season-ending event despite her gritty 6-4, 7-5 victory over Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk.
"Linda's such a great player," Pegula said. "Every time we've played, if you see the scoreline of our past matches, it's literally the same match every time... I knew I was going to get my chances.
"I felt like I did in the second, but then, you know, she's a Grand Slam champion, she's a great player and she did a great job to turn the match around.
"And then I had to do the same in the third," she added.
Noskova had already secured her semi-final spot with a pair of round-robin wins and she was on the brink of finishing with a perfect group record with a match point at 5-4 in the third.
Pegula escaped, firing an ace on game point, then broke Noskova in the next game. She closed out the win on her first match point.
Pegula finished second in the group behind Noskova and on Saturday will face group two winner Mirra Andreeva -- just a week after a microphone installed to capture "ambient sound" on a practice court caught Pegula describing the Russian teen as a "diva".
Andreeva said after her opening match that Pegula had reached out to apologize and she considered the matter closed.
Gauff had done what she could to stay alive.
Trailing 5-1 in the second set against Kostyuk she saved three set points in the seventh game to launch a run of six straight games to seize the match.
The first set had also been a battle. Broken in the opening game, Gauff appeared to have seized control when she broke Kostyuk for a second time for a 4-2 lead then held for 5-2.
Kostyuk looked demoralized as she took a medical timeout for treatment on her right wrist.
But after having the wrist taped she came back to hold serve then broke Gauff as the American served for the set -- Gauff helping her out with a pair of double faults.
Gauff regrouped to take the set, but surrendered two breaks to trail 3-0 in the second before receiving treatment for what she later said was back tightness.
Despite nine double faults, however, Gauff prevailed in one hour and 39 minutes.
Round-robin play concludes on Friday when world number two Aryna Sabalenka and sixth-ranked Ukrainian Elina Svitolina meet to decide the second qualifier from their group.
Andreeva will take on Czech Karolina Muchova, who has been eliminated from semi-final contention.

item.title: Scaloni to stay on as Argentina coach until 2030 World Cup
item.description:
Lionel Scaloni has agreed to extend his contract as head coach of Argentina's national team until the 2030 FIFA World Cup, the Argentine Football Association said on Thursday.
Scaloni, whose previous contract was due to expire in December, had been non-committal about his future after leading Argentina to this year's World Cup final.
"After giving it some thought and discussing it with my coaching staff and those close to me, we decided that continuing is the best path forward," the 48-year-old told a news conference.
Scaloni took charge of Argentina following its round-of-16 exit at the 2018 World Cup. With a new generation of players supporting experienced stars such as Lionel Messi and Angel Di Maria, Scaloni guided Argentina to the most successful era in its history, winning the 2021 and 2024 Copa America titles and the 2022 World Cup.
"I am grateful for all the expressions of affection," Scaloni said. "A huge part of the decision to continue was, without a doubt, the fans. I want to keep bringing them the joy they feel when watching the national team, and I hope that continues."
Earlier, AFA president Claudio Tapia described the announcement as a "joy for all Argentines".
"This is the best outcome for Argentine football; it's something everyone wanted, something we all wanted," Tapia said.
The new deal means Scaloni is on track to become the first manager to lead Argentina at three World Cups.
While optimistic about the future, he admitted the Albiceleste faced a period of transition following the international retirement of Messi last month. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner departed as Argentina's all-time leading scorer with 126 goals and most capped player with 208 appearances.
"An important phase in our process begins now. We will give opportunities to the youngsters who are pushing through the ranks," Scaloni said. "We need patience. They have enormous potential, but perhaps they aren't yet ready to deliver what the likes of Messi, Angel Di Maria, and Nicolas Otamendi provided."
He added: "I have the same drive I had on the very first day, the same enthusiasm, and I'm happy to be able to continue."

item.title: England reach Nations League quarters as Italy beat Zidane's France
item.description:
England secured their place in the Nations League quarter-finals with a 2-1 victory over Croatia on Thursday, while Zinedine Zidane suffered his first defeat as France coach as his side lost away to Italy.
Harry Kane marked his record-breaking 126th appearance for England by scoring the winning goal from the penalty spot at Wembley, taking his international tally to 92 goals.
Morgan Rogers put England ahead in the first half before a mistake by Jarell Quansah allowed Petar Sucic to equalise for Croatia on the hour mark.
England regained the lead when Ivan Smolcic wrestled Quansah to the ground at a corner, with Kane converting the resulting penalty after a VAR review.
Thomas Tuchel's side moved to 12 points from five matches in Group A3, ensuring they will go through to the quarter-finals next March.
"Good win. We wanted this win desperately and I think we deserved it," Tuchel told ITV.
"We got the job done and it was important because it was a special occasion for Harry and he scored the winner, so perfect evening."
Spain top the section on 15 points after a 2-0 win over the Czech Republic in Prague, their fifth straight victory in the competition.
Alex Baena's penalty and a late goal from Marc Pubill extended Spain's unbeaten run in competitive matches to 44 and set up a showdown with England in Madrid on Sunday, which will decide the group winners.
The Czechs remain without a point and finished with 10 men after captain Ladislav Krejci was sent off.
Italy came from behind to beat France 3-1 in Milan and hand Zidane his first defeat since taking charge of Les Bleus.
France were without Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele due to injury but Michael Olise pounced on a loose pass from Gianluigi Donnarumma to fire them ahead on 10 minutes.
Francesco Pio Esposito steered in Nicolo Cambiaghi's pass to bring Italy level before France twice hit the post through Bradley Barcola and Rayan Cherki.
Sebastiano Esposito blazed a second-half penalty wide for Italy, but Roberto Mancini's side did not rue that miss as Davide Frattesi powered home Federico Dimarco's cut-back.
Francesco Pio Esposito then doubled his tally for the night, succeeding where his older brother had failed by converting a penalty after Dayot Upamecano fouled substitute Antonio Vergara.
Zidane put the loss down to "part of the learning process".
"You mustn't change anything just because of a defeat," he said.
Italy climbed above France at the top of Group A1 on head-to-head record. Both teams have 10 points going into the final round of games, with Belgium just one point adrift.
Belgium host Italy on Sunday and France are at home to Turkey.
Zidane said Mbappe could return for the game in Bordeaux.
"I hope he'll be available on Sunday. That was the plan, that's what we want," he said.
Turkey slid to a fifth straight loss as they went down 2-1 to Belgium in Izmir.
Arda Guler's magnificent free-kick put Turkey ahead under new coach and former midfielder Sergen Yalcin, but Belgium struck twice in quick succession with goals from Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere to come away with victory.

item.title: Time to deliver to climate promises
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and UN General Assembly President Dr Khalilur Rahman both delivered what is an overdue message to the global community: The era of empty climate promises must end.
The prime minister rightly pointed out that climate-vulnerable nations require grants, not debt-inducing loans, all the while outlining five concrete actions to overhaul what must be called a broken international finance architecture.
Simultaneously, Dr Khalilur Rahman warned that the widening disparity between political pledges and real-world implementation has become an existential chasm, urging world leaders to make Antalya the "COP of implementation."
Nowhere is the hypocrisy displayed by the developed world more damaging than across developing countries of the Global South, and on the frontlines of our own country.
While global carbon emissions surged to a record 42 billion tons last year and warming trajectories hurtle toward 2.8 degrees Celsius for this century, developing economies continue bearing the catastrophic brunt of a crisis they did not create.
Bangladesh itself contributes less than 0.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet our coastal communities, river systems, and agricultural yields are being systematically dismantled by rising seas, salinity intrusion, and relentless cyclones.
The financial arithmetic outlined in Antalya lays bare the moral failure of major industrial polluters. Developing countries require up to $305 billion annually merely to adapt to climate fallout, yet international adaptation funding languishes at a paltry $26bn. As the UNGA president aptly noted, that shortfall is not a rounding error but a verdict on global solidarity.
If COP31 is to mean anything, wealthy nations must immediately honour their historical obligations. More international climate finance must be dedicated directly to adaptation, distributed as predictable grants based on vulnerability rather than arbitrary income classifications.
Antalya must not become another venue for hollow declarations. Major carbon-emitting powers must abandon stalling tactics and deliver the finance and action required to safeguard nations such as Bangladesh in the developing world.

item.title: Russia says no decision on letting Europe join Ukraine talks
item.description:
Russia said Friday it had not yet agreed to let Europeans join US-mediated talks on ending the war in Ukraine, after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and American envoy Jared Kushner said Europe would take part in the next round.
During talks held in Abu Dhabi earlier this week, European envoys held separate meetings with the Ukrainian delegation but did not participate in the US-led meetings between Kyiv and Moscow teams.
After a debrief with the US envoys, Zelensky said Europeans would take part in the next talks, while Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, said a peace deal could not be concluded “without Europeans being at the table.”
But the Kremlin indicated it had not yet agreed.
“Once we understand their real intentions and their willingness to contribute to the peace process, then we can make a decision on holding talks in an expanded format,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.
“If the Europeans really do have someone who is at least authorized in some way to talk, and if the Europeans really do have the desire to do so, then, of course, we will be ready to talk to them,” Peskov said.
Russia’s lead negotiator in Abu Dhabi, Vladimir Medinsky, said after the latest trilateral meeting that Moscow had “not received a single peace initiative or a single concrete peace proposal from European countries.”
It was “unclear what there is to discuss” with Europe, he added.

item.title: India blocks over 100 speakers from opposition democracy summit
item.description:
India blocked more than 100 international speakers from attending a democracy summit organized by the opposition Congress party, a senior opposition politician said on Friday.
Those denied visas included a Norwegian journalist who had previously questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi about press freedom.
Shashi Tharoor, a Congress MP and former senior United Nations official, said 115 of the 315 speakers cleared by India’s foreign ministry were subsequently refused entry or had their visas cancelled, “apparently on the instructions” of the home ministry.
“It is completely unclear under what provision of law the government has taken such a drastic step,” Tharoor wrote on X.
“What a shame that a proud democracy has become so insecure that it must stifle any voices it fears will be critical!” he added.
Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng said on Wednesday that her visa was cancelled shortly before she was due to travel to India, where she had been invited to speak on media and press freedom.
She had questioned Modi at a press briefing during his visit to Oslo in May.
The Editors Guild of India condemned the cancellation and said the move smacked of “bureaucratic overreach” and called on the government to disclose its reasons and reverse the decision.
The two-day summit, which opened on Friday in the city of Hyderabad, brings together around 1,000 delegates from more than 70 countries to discuss democracy, climate change, artificial intelligence and global cooperation.
India’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.

item.title: Trump says US does not ‘need’ Iran deal and tells Vance to focus on Democratic fraud
item.description:
Donald Trump says the US does not need a deal with Iran and has directed Vice-President JD Vance, who has played a role in efforts to resolve the war, to focus “his complete and total attention” on alleged crime and corruption in Democratic-run cities and states.
Mr Trump’s directive came a day after The Wall Street Journal reported that Mr Vance was considering face-to-face peace talks with a hard-line Iranian security official and a week after the vice-president blamed the costly war with Iran for Republicans’ midterm elections drubbing.
Mr Trump’s comments marked a shift in tone after he had suggested in recent weeks that Iran would be more willing to strike a deal in the eight-month conflict after the US elections.
“We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Mr Trump wrote on social media, referring to the Strait of Hormuz, the critical shipping route near Iran where the US military has been working to secure safe passage for international shipping.
Mr Trump said he asked Mr Vance to focus instead on a domestic issue the president previously put in his portfolio: leading an effort targeting alleged fraud in Democratic-run cities and states throughout the US.
“Our Budget could be quickly BALANCED with the correction of this large-scale criminal activity. CORRUPTION is in the Democrat Leadership’s blood!” Mr Trump wrote on Thursday, local time.
Mr Vance’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Mr Vance was considering meeting with a senior Iranian security official, a move that would have put Mr Vance at the center of peace negotiations. Reuters has not confirmed the potential talks.
Mr Vance, who is viewed as a leading contender for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, distanced himself from the war last week after Republicans’ midterm election rout by Democrats.
The vice-president blamed the costs of the Iran war in part for the party’s losses. He also said an earlier recommendation to end the war was “sound advice.”
Mr Trump responded to Mr Vance’s position by defending the war as necessary to stop Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

item.title: Kerry sees US climate comeback as states and businesses defy Trump’s retreat
item.description:
Former US climate envoy John Kerry has expressed confidence that the United States will eventually return to a leading role in global climate action, arguing that the country's clean energy transition is continuing despite the Trump administration's withdrawal from international climate cooperation.
Speaking at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya on Tuesday, Kerry criticised the administration's efforts to roll back environmental protections, promote fossil fuels and undermine renewable energy.
He said the federal government's political direction did not reflect the broader momentum for clean energy across the United States.
“We will build and rebuild our partnerships,” Kerry said, expressing hope that the US would re-engage with international climate efforts in the future.
Kerry, who served as US secretary of state under former president Barack Obama and as President Joe Biden's special presidential envoy for climate, signed the Paris Agreement on behalf of the United States in 2016.
The US withdrawal from the Paris Agreement took effect on January 27, 2026, marking another retreat by the world's largest historical emitter from international climate cooperation.
However, Kerry said state and local governments, as well as private businesses, were continuing to invest in clean energy, creating jobs and generating economic benefits across political boundaries.
He noted that renewable energy and other low-carbon technologies were attracting investment in both Republican- and Democratic-led states.
Speaking to journalists on the sidelines of the summit, Kerry also urged climate advocates to change how they communicate the urgency of climate action.
“I think everybody who is working on climate needs to change the way they talk about it,” he said.
He argued that climate change should not be presented solely as an environmental or scientific issue. Instead, advocates should highlight its implications for employment, public health, national security, food supplies and community stability.
Kerry also took part in an energy transition discussion with former US vice-president Al Gore on Tuesday, highlighting the need to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and expand investment in clean energy.
He stressed that electrification alone would not guarantee emissions reductions, noting that its climate benefits would depend on how electricity was generated.
If rising electricity demand continued to be met by coal and natural gas, electrification could fail to deliver the expected emissions reductions, he cautioned.
His remarks came as United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres urged world leaders to accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels.
Addressing leaders at COP31 on Wednesday, Guterres challenged the influence of fossil fuel interests in climate policymaking.
“Fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs,” he said. “The dinosaurs did not have a lobby. Fossil fuels do.”
Guterres called for a “climate justice compact” to strengthen international cooperation, mobilise climate finance and protect communities facing the worst effects of global warming.
He also proposed taxing the windfall profits of major oil companies to help finance support for countries suffering climate-related losses and damage.
The proposal reflects growing frustration among climate-vulnerable countries over the gap between international commitments and the financial support reaching communities most exposed to climate change.
For developing countries such as Bangladesh, predictable climate financing is essential to protect coastal communities, agricultural livelihoods, infrastructure and public health.
At COP28 in Dubai in 2023, countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems in a just, orderly and equitable manner. However, translating that commitment into national policies, investment and measurable emissions reductions remains a major challenge.
Countries continue to differ over the pace of the transition, the role of natural gas and the financial responsibilities of developed and developing economies.
Kerry's remarks at COP31 highlighted how climate leadership may extend beyond national governments to businesses, local authorities, investors and civil society. His expectation of renewed US engagement offered a note of optimism, even as negotiations continue over climate finance and stronger action to reduce emissions.
This story was produced as part of the COP31 Climate Change Media Partnership, a journalism fellowship organised by Internews' Earth Journalism Network, Informed Earth and the Stanley Center for Peace and Security.

item.title: 291,209 applications seek HSC script re-evaluation, Dhaka board receives highest
item.description:
A total of 291,209 students have applied for re-scrutiny and re-evaluation of 1,087,413 answer scripts in various subjects under all 11 education boards following the publication of this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examination results.
Among the 11 education boards, Dhaka Education Board received the highest number of applications for answer script re-scrutiny, followed by Chittagong Education Board.
According to board-wise statistics, the highest 335,879 applications were submitted to the Dhaka Education Board, while the Chittagong Education Board received the second-highest number of applications, totaling 117,700.
Among the other boards, Rajshahi received 109,971 applications, Jessore 97,618, Comilla 92,776, Dinajpur 89,420, Mymensingh 71,762, Barisal 53,409, Sylhet 51,243, Madrasah Education Board 40,830 and Technical Education Board 26,806 applications for re-scrutiny of answer scripts.
Speaking to BSS on the issue, President of the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee and Chairman of the Dhaka Education Board Professor Syed Akhtaruzzaman said the examination and assessment systems had been made fully objective and impartial over the past two years.
He said answer scripts had been evaluated according to a prescribed set of standards, and the same method had also been followed last year.
Following the recent publication of HSC results, it was found that students had performed poorly in compulsory subjects such as English, Bangla and ICT across all education boards.
He said the failure rate in these subjects was also high. Taking into consideration the comparatively poor results and the high number of failures, the education boards had already started working on the matter.
Identifying the shortage of teachers as a major reason behind the poor results, he said, "Many colleges do not have sufficient ICT teachers. Even in government colleges, teachers from other disciplines are assigned to teach ICT due to the absence of subject-specific teachers."
Subject-wise statistics of the Dhaka Education Board show that a large number of applications for answer script re-scrutiny have been submitted not only in Bangla, English and ICT but also in important subjects under the Science, Humanities and Business Studies groups.
According to the statistics, an equal number of 42,002 applications were submitted for English First Paper and Second Paper, while 38,075 applications were received for Information and Communication Technology (ICT).
These two subjects recorded the highest numbers of answer script re-scrutiny applications under the Dhaka Education Board.
An analysis of the statistics shows that, alongside English, a significant number of applications were also submitted for re-scrutiny of Bangla answer scripts among the compulsory subjects.
An equal number of 24,858 applications were submitted for Bangla First Paper and Second Paper.
Among the important Science group subjects, Chemistry received the highest number of applications, with an equal 18,482 applications for both First Paper and Second Paper.
Besides, an equal number of 15,757 applications were submitted for re-scrutiny of Biology answer scripts in both First Paper and Second Paper.
In the Humanities group, an equal 3,571 applications were submitted for Civics and Good Governance First Paper and Second Paper, while 1,997 applications were received for Social Work.
Among the Business Studies group subjects, Accounting received the highest number of applications.
An equal 3,827 applications were submitted for Accounting First Paper and Second Paper.
Besides, 2,331 applications were received for re-scrutiny of Business Organization and Management answer scripts.
The Ministry of Education said the pass rate in the HSC and equivalent examinations, the results of which were published on October 31, stood at 52.12 percent across the 11 education boards.
Of the total 1,240,798 examinees, 646,685 students passed, while 40,084 secured GPA-5.
Failing to achieve their expected results, 291,209 students under the 11 boards applied for re-scrutiny of 1,087,413 answer scripts.
The deadline for submitting applications was 12 noon on November 8.
Sources at the Ministry of Education and education boards said significant changes had also been observed following the re-scrutiny of this year's SSC and equivalent examination results.
Of the total 1,829,485 examinees under the 11 education boards in the SSC and equivalent examinations, 402,052 students applied for re-evaluation of their results, involving a total of 1,287,926 answer scripts.
Following re-scrutiny, a total of 4,585 students across the country who had initially failed in the SSC examinations passed, while another 3,079 students secured GPA-5.
The Inter-Education Board authorities said strict disciplinary action would also be taken against the concerned examiners and chief examiners if major inconsistencies in answer script assessment or significant discrepancies in marks were found during the HSC re-evaluation, as had happened in the SSC examinations.
President of the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee Professor Syed Akhtaruzzaman said more than a hundred examiners and chief examiners had been identified for major deviations in answer script assessment during the SSC examinations.
He said specific diagnostic assessments were being conducted on their cases and recommendations for disciplinary action were being sent to the Ministry of Education.
If similar cases of unjustified marking or excessive differences in marks were found during the HSC result re-scrutiny, recommendations would be made for disciplinary action against the examiners and chief examiners responsible for negligence in assessing answer scripts, following the same procedure.
He made it clear that inappropriate or faulty assessment would primarily be determined by examining the difference between the marks obtained by a student before and after re-scrutiny. Necessary action would be taken accordingly.
According to the action plan of the Inter-Education Board, after receiving students' applications for re-scrutiny of HSC and equivalent examination results through the website, the application data will be collected from the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET).
Subsequently, the Computer Cell will send lists containing answer script information and subject-wise details to the relevant sections. Examiners will be appointed for re-evaluation, and answer scripts will be collected from the chief examiners.
In the next phase, re-evaluation work will begin following a briefing for the appointed examiners.
It was further stated that after completing the assessment, the statements signed by the re-evaluation examiners, along with the answer scripts whose marks have been changed, will be sent to the Computer Cell.
The Computer Cell will then enter the revised marks and verify the litho codes of the answer scripts. Following the final verification of the revised answer scripts, the results of the re-scrutiny and re-evaluation will be published.
The Dhaka Education Board said the re-scrutiny process for this year's HSC examination answer scripts had begun.
The process started on November 11 with the participation of examiners and concerned officials.
It will continue until November 17, from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm every day, at the Higher Secondary Examination Section on the seventh and eighth floors of Building No. 4 of the board.
Senior System Analyst of the Dhaka Education Board, Engineer Md. Monjurul Kabir, told BSS that the processing of hundreds of thousands of online applications and related data submitted for HSC answer script re-scrutiny would be carried out with utmost caution.
He said the board's ICT team was closely monitoring the entire process to ensure that no inconsistencies occurred in the changes to marks following publication of the results.

item.title: ‘Rokzana’ singer Shaikh Shahed Ali no more
item.description:
Musician Shaikh Shahed Ali, best known for the song "Rokzana" has passed away while undergoing treatment at a hospital.
He passed away at 10:05am on Friday.
The news of his death was confirmed by the late singer's friend Ershadul Haque Tinku.
Shaikh Shahed Ali was a familiar name in Bangladesh's band music scene in the 1990s. He had been seriously ill for some time and was receiving treatment at Azgar Ali Hospital in the capital.
Shahed was admitted to hospital on October 24 after his blood sodium levels dropped. While undergoing treatment, he suffered a mild stroke and also tested positive for dengue.
As his condition deteriorated, he was transferred to Azgar Ali Hospital via Square Hospital. The musician had also been undergoing regular dialysis for the past four years due to kidney complications.
His illness put on hold plans to release 24 new songs, which he had worked on over 11 years.
The musician had been scheduled to release four CDs, cassettes and vinyl records on November 6.
The founder of the band "Gachh" Shaikh Shahed, won over listeners with songs such as "Rokzana", "Upolobdhi," "Khola Chul" and "Prem Ashbei."
His debut album, "Probhu", was released in 1991.
